projects.name: Tension Fibers
projects.goal: Hold up the 3 middle road joints with cables from the two masts.
projects.tip: Click a mast top, then a road joint, to hang a cable. Cables can only pull.
projects.lesson: A cable is pulled tight (tension). Its pull T holds the road up: T sin(angle) = load.

steps.text: Hang a cable from the left mast top to road joint 1.
Hang a cable from the left mast top to the middle road joint.
Hang a cable from the right mast top to road joint 3.

hints: Cables can only pull. Each road joint between the banks needs one cable pulling it up.
Join a mast top (the joints high on the banks) to the road joints 1, 2 and 3.
Size S is strong enough for a car - save your parts.

projects.name: Coplanar Trusses
projects.goal: Build a truss: a top chord and diagonals so every panel is a triangle.
projects.tip: A square can fold flat; a triangle cannot. Join every top joint so it makes triangles.
projects.lesson: Triangles keep their shape. Members are pulled (tension) or pushed (compression); pushed long thin members buckle: P_cr = pi^2 E I / L^2.

steps.text: Build the top chord: join the five top joints in a line.
Add the two end posts from the supports up to the top. They carry the most, so use size L.
Add a vertical under every top joint.
Add diagonals sloping down towards the middle, so every panel is a triangle.

hints: A frame of squares folds flat. Every panel needs a diagonal to make two triangles.
Start with the top chord, then the end posts, verticals and diagonals.
If an end post buckles, make it size L - long pushed members buckle first.

projects.name: Parabolic Thrust
projects.goal: Build the arch rib from bank to bank, hang the road from it, and brace it.
projects.tip: Arches are pushed (compression): steel or concrete. A moving truck can make a cable hanger go slack - steel hangers can push and pull. Add a few diagonal braces.
projects.lesson: A parabolic arch carries an even load in pure compression; it pushes outward on both banks (thrust H = w L^2 / 8h), so both supports must be pinned.

steps.text: Build the arch rib from bank to bank through the arch joints (steel, size L).
Hang the road from the arch: a steel hanger from each arch joint straight down.
Brace the arch with diagonals so it cannot change shape.

hints: The arch must go from bank to bank through all the arch joints, and it is pushed (compression).
Cable hangers can go slack when the truck lifts the arch - steel hangers push and pull.
Brace the arch: diagonals between arch joints and the road joints next to them.

projects.name: Stay Dynamics
projects.goal: Cable-stay the road from one tall pylon. Balance the cables on both sides.
projects.tip: Anchor the pylon top with a backstay cable to each bank support, then put matching cables left and right. Flat cables need a bigger size.
projects.lesson: A flat cable needs a bigger pull for the same lift: T = W / sin(angle). The horizontal parts of the stays must balance at the pylon top.

steps.text: Anchor the pylon top with a backstay cable to each bank support.
Fan stays from the pylon top to the left half of the road.
Mirror the fan on the right half so the pulls balance.

hints: Without backstays the pylon top can sway: tie it to both bank supports first.
Then give every road joint its own stay, balanced left and right.
Flat stays near the banks pull hardest; use size M or bigger.

projects.name: Matrix Dissipation
projects.goal: Two pylons, a long span and a heavy convoy with 30% impact. Use parts wisely.
projects.tip: Anchor each pylon top to its bank, tie the two tops together, and share the middle span between both pylons. Carbon cable is stronger for the same size.
projects.lesson: Impact (dynamic) load = 1.3 x static. The stiffness matrix [K][U] = [F] shares the load between all members in proportion to their stiffness E A / L.

steps.text: Anchor each pylon top to its bank support.
Tie the two pylon tops together.
Fan carbon stays from the left pylon over its side of the road.
Fan carbon stays from the right pylon; road joint 8 in the middle gets one from each pylon.

hints: Each pylon top needs a backstay to its bank, and a tie to the other pylon top.
Every road joint needs a stay; the middle joint can take one from each pylon.
Carbon cable is stronger for the same size. Watch the stays near the banks.
